developer_values.write_block rewrites the whole file by read-modify-write: it reads the file (:60), writes a fixed temp `<file>.tmp` (:84-85) and renames it over the target with Path.replace, which is os.replace (:86). It takes no lock, calls no fsync, copies no file mode and removes no temp on failure.

write_block keeps every top-level line except a header written exactly `developer:`; it drops every indented or blank line under that header (comments included) and the trailing blank lines; on Windows the rewritten file has CRLF line ends because write_text gets no newline argument.

A header `developer:  # note` or `developer: {}` is not recognised: the old block stays and write_block appends a second `developer:` block, so afk-config parse raises `duplicate key 'developer'` and every later load of that layer fails. A column-0 comment inside the block leaves the following indented lines orphaned, and parse fails with `could not parse the rest of the file`.

On Windows, two processes running record()'s read_block plus write_block 200 times each on one file lose updates and fail: one landed 1 of 200 writes, the other 196, with 203 PermissionError (WinError 5) from the shared temp name and os.replace. With a reader polling the file, the reader got PermissionError on 1403 of 40649 reads and a stale `race.yaml.tmp` stayed. No torn file was observed.

developer_values main catches only ValueError and ConfigError, so an OSError from the replace (for example WinError 5 while another process has the file open) ends `set` with a traceback and leaves `config.yaml.tmp` beside the target.

The readers of both files are afk-config layers and load: a missing machine or repository file is skipped (is_file), but a present file that does not parse raises ConfigError out of load, so a malformed developer block breaks every reader of that layer. The one caller of `set` is the agent following MANIFEST.md H6 step 4, once per path in sequence.
A live reader never sees a half-written developer file because os.replace swaps whole files; after a power loss the renamed file may be empty or stale because nothing calls fsync before the rename.

claims.text: The occupancy and meter writers run from harness hook events: SessionStart runs protected-branch-occupancy.py, PreToolUse runs protected-branch-guard.py (occupancy.claim, change_meter.record_pre, main_sync.authorize), PostToolUse runs protected-branch-meter.py (change_meter.after), each with a 30 s timeout in both manifests
No shared atomic-write or file-lock helper is imported across modules; each writer carries its own copy.
skills/afk/setup/scripts/install_block.py _target_lock + _atomic_write_locked is the only writer combining an OS lock, compare-and-swap, fsync and mode preservation.
developer_values.write_block and setup_secrets.write_json_atomic use a fixed temp name and no lock, so two concurrent runs can lose an update or clash on the temp.
lesson-append.sh allocates L-NNNN by reading the max id then appending, with no lock, so two concurrent opened events can share an id.
afk-config.py init writes .afk/config.yaml in place with no temp file.

On this Windows machine os.replace and Path.replace onto a file another process holds open with Python's default open() raise PermissionError (WinError 5) and succeed once it closes; os.rename onto an existing file raises FileExistsError (WinError 183); a reader racing a replace loop saw no torn content but got PermissionError opens.

Two concurrent developer_values set runs on one file lost 50 to 80 of 100 updates in three trials, failing with PermissionError WinError 32, WinError 5 and errno 13 rather than FileNotFoundError; main() catches only ValueError and ConfigError, so those surface as tracebacks.

write_block drops comments inside the developer block and trailing value comments, moves the block to the end of the file and rewrites it with CRLF line ends on Windows; a header written as 'developer:  # note' is not recognised, so the write appends a second developer block and the file stops parsing (duplicate key).

Concurrent Git Bash printf >> appends of 37-byte lines did not tear in 2000 appends, but 4103-byte lines tore 36 to 68 times per 1000; a lesson-append event carrying a long --draft is in the tearing range.

Writers of settings files outside the named scope write in place with no temp: set_instruction_files.py rewrites the Claude settings file in place, remove-worktree.py adopt() rewrites the worktree owner record in place while worktree_owner.py writes the same record through a temp and os.replace, and update-notice, app-start-gate, worktree-provision, notes note-update and the investigate ledger writers also write in place.

Five lock mechanisms exist, each private to its file: occupancy.py O_EXCL lock file with 10 s stale takeover, install_block.py and bounded_scan.py msvcrt/fcntl kernel locks, create-worktree and maven-lock.sh mkdir locks.

No reusable atomic-write or lock helper exists for a new writer to import; install_block.write_if_unchanged is the most complete implementation (OS lock, compare-and-swap, unique temp, fsync, mode) and is the natural one to extract, but nothing outside its own file and its test calls it today.

Nothing pins write_block under concurrency, with comments inside the block, or with a commented header; nothing pins write_json_atomic's write; nothing pins lesson-append id allocation under concurrency; install_block, occupancy, create-worktree, bounded_scan, protected-lookup, forge_ledger and lavish inject do have lock or failed-replace tests.

setup_secrets.write_json_atomic shares write_block's fixed-temp, no-lock shape, so the concurrency loss measured for write_block applies to it; it was not run concurrently here because it is an interactive script.
